item.text: PORT-010 keeps reporting a production #[cfg(unix)] function with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback. Evidence: test port010_real_gap_still_reported passes, showing one finding for that fixture.
item.title: ANC-009 pass fixture

item.text: PORT-010 now skips every #[cfg(unix)] item in a file once any Windows code exists anywhere in that file.
item.title: ANC-009 fail fixture

item.text: In crates/sc-lint-portability, PORT-010 does not report an item carrying #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason = "...")]; the reason is required, and the allowance covers only that item, not its module, file or siblings. An unannotated production #[cfg(unix)] item with no #[cfg(windows)] companion and no portable fallback is still reported.
item.title: PORT-010 per-site allowance

cases.rationale: ANC-009 v2 scope: 'The item changes when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] item.' INTENT (cut 2026-10-31): 'Other shapes use reasoned site allowances; unallowed real parity gaps still report' and ANC-010 v3 (locked): an item carrying #[sc_lint(allow(PORT-010), reason)] is not reported. A reasoned single-item allowance is therefore not blanket suppression.

item.text: In crates/sc-lint-portability, PORT-010 does not report a #[cfg(unix)] item with a same-name #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling in the same module. A #[cfg(unix)] item with no companion and no portable fallback is still reported (negative tests).
item.title: PORT-010 same-name siblings

cases.rationale: ANC-009 v2 scope: 'The item changes when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] item.' Narrow companion recognition that keeps real gaps reported.
